answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it may transact, released only after a sustained record of honest work. Every agent emits a regular heartbeat pulse proving liveness and continued control of its kernel credentials, and identities that miss pulses or behave inconsistently forfeit part of their stake. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital locked per identity plus ongoing compute to keep each pulse alive, so an attacker pays linearly for every fake agent while honest agents pay once.
